content.title: About
content.content: Potato French Fries with Chili are deep‑fried potato sticks tossed in a spicy sauce made from chili peppers, spices, and sometimes tomato paste. The dish is a staple of fast‑food restaurants and street vendors, offering a crunchy, hot snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: French fries originated in the United States in the early 20th century and quickly became an iconic fast‑food item.
The chili sauce often uses jalapeño, serrano, or cayenne peppers, giving the dish varying levels of heat.
In some countries the fries are served with cheese sauce, but the classic chili version relies solely on the spicy topping.
Traditionally the potatoes are cut into 0.5–1 cm sticks to achieve a crisp exterior and a soft interior.
The dish is commonly served in cardboard containers, making it easy to eat on the go.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potatoes provide potassium, which supports normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: B‑vitamins source
items.content: Potatoes contain vitamin B6 and B3, important for metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Antioxidants in chili
items.content: Capsaicin and other compounds in chili have antioxidant properties that help protect cells.

items.title: Metabolism boost
items.content: Spicy foods can temporarily increase thermogenesis, aiding calorie burning.

items.title: Improved digestion
items.content: Spices in the sauce may stimulate gastric juice production, supporting digestion.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Deep‑fried potatoes and oily sauce make the dish calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Spiciness of chili
items.content: Very hot peppers can cause heartburn or stomach irritation in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some people may be allergic to potatoes or ingredients in the sauce.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Salt added during frying and in the sauce raises sodium intake, which is a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the fries hot, typically in a paper container or on a plate. Eat with fingers, a fork, or dip them in additional sauce. For a lighter option, choose baked fries and a milder chili sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared fries are best consumed within 2–3 hours at room temperature. For longer storage, cool them to room temperature, then place in an airtight container in the refrigerator (up to 24 hours). Reheat in an oven to restore crispness.
